chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My Honour and My Majesty! I will not take a servant from the world while I intend to be merciful to him until I fully compensate him for every mistake (sin) he has committed, either through sickness in his body, or through constriction in his sustenance, or through fear in his worldly life. So if a remainder remains upon him, I will intensify (the punishment) for him at the time of death.'

And by My Honour and My Majesty! I will not take a servant from the world while I intend to punish him until I fully fulfill for him every good deed he has done, either through expansion in his sustenance, or through health in his body, or through security in his worldly life. So if a remainder remains upon him, I will ease the death for him because of it.'
ai.seo_question: How does God compensate for sins and reward good deeds in this world before death?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, recorded in al-Kafi, elucidates the concept of 'Hastening of Punishment' (Tasri' al-'Iqab) by framing worldly afflictions as expiatory mechanisms for sins and worldly blessings as deferred rewards for the wicked. Scholarly tradition interprets this as a manifestation of divine mercy, where the believer's minor sins are purged through physical or financial trials, ensuring a cleaner state at death. The text highlights the dual nature of divine justice, where the balance of deeds is settled either through immediate worldly experience or at the moment of transition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “By My<sup>azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup>azwj</sup> will not Exit a servant from the world and I<sup>azwj</sup> want to be Merciful to him until I<sup>azwj</sup> Fulfil every mistake (sin) from him which he has done, either by a sickness in his body, and either by constriction in his sustenance, and either by fear in his world. So if there remains upon him a remainder, I<sup>azwj</sup> would Intensify upon him (pangs) during the death.

And by My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty! I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> will not Exit a servant from the world and I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Want to Punish him until I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Fulfill for him every good deed that he has done, either by Expansion in his sustenance, and either by good healthy body, and either by security in this world. So if there remains upon him a remainder, I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall Ease the death upon him due to it”’’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘I swear by My Majesty and Glory, I will not take out of this world a servant whom I want to receive mercy until I will compensate from him for all the sins that he has committed. (I will do so) by causing illness in his body, constraint in the means of his living or fear for his worldly affairs. If anything is left to offset this I will cause his death to be a severe suffering.’

“I swear by My Majesty and Glory that I will not take out of this world a servant whom I want to be punished until I will fully compensate him for his good deeds in this world. This I will do either by expanding the means of his living, granting him good health in his body or by grating him peace in this world and if anything will be left without compensation I will cause his death to take place with ease.’”
